articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football All-Bust Team: Second-year players, 1 trendy sleeper among those to be cautious when drafting
articles.summary: These players comprise a team that we are  avoiding in drafts for 2026 fantasy football.
articles.body:
You can't beat a good thriller movie. Seven, Zodiac, The Shining … the list keeps going. They're all classics. And keep the viewer (me) locked into the plot, not just by the actors giving standout performances. But the clues sprinkled throughout the sequences. Tidbits of info that come together like pieces of a puzzle all at once when the time is right.

For us, that time is now. We've walked through every phase of the draft. Isolated profiles of what busts look like. You've even got a list of players to avoid based on their ADP. Now, let's put it all together. We're going to assemble the All-Bust Team of the 2026 season.

We never talked about identifying busts at the QB position. Partly because their ADPs are sparse and the same mechanisms (e.g., change in scheme, added competition) for our core positions don't apply. But I did find a way to hone in on when we should be the most cautious when drafting our starting passer.

I used the same scaled-threshold approach as in our early-round discussion . Failing to meet expectations relative to draft price highlights where waiting on QB has its merits. In either case, the QB1-4 and QB5-8 buckets hold the most risk.

So, I'll be honest. Looking at Yahoo's ADP , Joe Burrow (QB4) sticks out with the highest bust potential relative to his peers. All the rest have mobility in their game. But I'm a (long-suffering) Bengals fan. As a result, I shifted to the next cluster and found a suitable replacement.

Jaxson Dart's mobility and off-script throwing talent were instant attention-grabbers. He finished the season with top-five marks in rushing yards and TDs. After seeing his college tape, that's exactly what drafters wanted. But without the Konami Code, Dart's throwing ability would've left us with more questions than answers.

Completion Percentage Over Expected: -0.2%, 20th

Dart fell below the league average across every efficiency metric. Even his pressure-to-sack ratio was seventh-worst. His trips to the blue tent should also be a concern to drafters. But let's assume he stays healthy. We still have the health of his WR1 to consider.

Malik Nabers' slow ramp-up has been positive throughout the course of the offseason. But there are still question marks about his Week 1 availability. And a cast of role players, along with 33-year-old Odell Beckham Jr., are backing up Nabers. Between Dart's own health and the availability of his pass-catchers, Dart is the first to make the All-Bust Team.

New Orleans handed Etienne real money this offseason. What the Saints didn't hand him was a role that actually uses him.

Now, I'll walk this call back if offensive coordinator Doug Nussmeier's assessment of his new RB (as a receiver/running back) turns into a reliable target share. But this is HC Kellen Moore's offense. And it hasn't prioritized rushers as pass-game options in the past.

Over the past five seasons, Moore's playcalling has left rushers in the bottom half of the league in target rate. And that's across all players at the position. Not just the starter. Which brings us to the other issue for Etienne.

The backfield split didn't resolve as most expected. After what appeared to be a farewell tour, Alvin Kamara is back for another year. Sure, he's already nursing an injury. But it's hard to see Etienne picking up the third-down, two-minute role with a savvy vet like Kamara on the sideline. Accordingly, the former Jaguar profiles as the type of RB with a fragile workload we should avoid.

Judkins looks like a workhorse on paper. On tape and in the numbers, the details get murkier.

Now, I get it. I'm highlighting a single game against a divisional rival. Fans would argue that I'm stacking the deck against him. OK, fine. I'll expand the scope of the argument to the entire season.

Rushing Success Rate: 31.6%, 19th (out of 19 qualifiers – min. 50% of team rush atts.)

Well, to be fair, I zoomed in on Weeks 3-15. Essentially, a game after he got up to speed (started in Week 2) and before he got injured in Week 16. And during that time, only Jonathan Taylor had a higher share of his team's totes. But more volume didn't equate to more productive touches.

The Browns' rookie had the fourth-most carries but the 13th-most yards. Rico Dowdle generated 213 more than Judkins, while splitting time with Chuba Hubbard. And if the Browns' QB situation has you concerned (and it should), Judkins' outlook for '26 is one we should let our leaguemates acquire.

Drafters at the 1-2 turn will have a hard time passing up Nico Collins.

And honestly, there's no obvious reason to consider anyone else. Over the past two seasons, Collins is one of eight receivers with back-to-back seasons over 2.0 YPRR. And just one of four to do it with a receiving aDOT over 10 air yards. However, he's not the one I'm worried about.

EPA per Dropback: 7th (2023 – among all starters), 27th (2024), 13th

We haven't seen C.J. Stroud get back to the heights he achieved in his rookie season. Houston's playoff game against New England officially put us on "Stroud Watch." On the one hand, we should be interested after the Texans acquired veteran offensive linemen and used Day 1 draft capital to bolster Stroud's protection. But the loss of WR Jayden Higgins, while boosting Collins' projected target share, lessens the versatility of the passing game. So, while betting on talent is the right approach in the early rounds, the ability of the receiver and their QB should be on our minds.

I'm not sure what a bell-cow receiver is. But I'm into it.

If any WR is deserving of the title, it's Garrett Wilson. Since entering the league in '22, if Wilson's been on the field for more than 10 games, his target shares have been no less than 25.0%. The former Buckeye has averaged 8.7, 9.9, and 9.1 looks per game. And 2025 didn't start any different (9.3), but a hyperextended knee sidelined him for the remainder of the season.

However, there's a problem. That high-end workload didn't matter.

2022: 12.7 (PPR PPG), 28th (min. 10 games)

For reference, Wilson's 2026 ADP sits at WR20. He's finished ahead of that just once. The rest of the time, he's been in the high-end WR3 discussion. The excuse has always been quarterback play, and it's not an unfair one — but the new answer isn't obviously better. Geno Smith has never led a wide receiver to a 15+ PPG season across six years as a starter.

The Jets also added two first-round rookies (Omar Cooper Jr., Kenyon Sadiq) to a receiving corps that didn't need more mouths to feed. Wilson's talent has never been the question. The problem is that gaudy target shares keep not showing up on the scoreboard, and there's no clear reason 2026 breaks that pattern.

Oh, wait. We've got the other onesie position. Just like in the QB conversation, I used the same approach to find where bust rates are likely to occur based on draft cost.

Again, we're looking for guys that can pay off their pre-season ADP. Luckily, the early-round players pay off more often than not. However, it's that middle class of TEs that let us down. And, of course, the guy I took in our expert league immediately stood out.

When healthy, Kraft's per-catch numbers are legitimately special.

However, the Packers are already telling us they're not fully sure he'll be on the field enough to matter. Now, it's fair to question how much of the truth the Packers are telling us. But it's hard to lie with your wallet.

Signing a proven, 10-year veteran receiving tight end this late in camp isn't a depth move for the No. 3 spot. It's insurance for exactly the scenario where Kraft can't handle a full workload. And reports already suggest Green Bay plans to use both in 12-personnel sets, capping Kraft's target monopoly even in games he's fully healthy.

He's still the clear TE1 in Green Bay. But drafting him as a top-five tight end means betting against both his own recent multi-ligament knee injury and a front office that just paid real money to hedge against it.

I've mentioned this before, but I usually root for the underdog. The guy that most folks overlook. And players who earned late-round draft capital but rise in popularity will always have my support.

All the way up until I have to pay extra to draft them.

Parker Washington's second half of 2025 was special. It helped keep Jacksonville in the playoff picture. However, the circumstances behind his ascension are the part getting glossed over.

Target Rate: 11.1% (Weeks 11-14), 24.4% (Weeks 15-18)

First, Washington's climb up the pecking order happened over four weeks. Yes, we saw double-digit target outings from him earlier in the season (Weeks 3 and 7). But the peaks didn't outweigh the valleys. It wasn't until this short window (the most important time of the season) that we saw the breakout. And that same scenario may be hard to replicate in '26.

Washington's target-share explosion happened when the receiver room was missing its top-two guys, Travis Hunter and Brian Thomas Jr. Hunter is healthy again, even if he's leaning more toward defense by design. And Thomas is good to go. Plus, Jakobi Meyers and Brenton Strange, both real target earners in their own right, never left.

The bullish case treats Washington's role as settled. Drafters are acting as if he's the unquestioned WR1. However, when you consider that his breakout occurred against a depleted depth chart, it's a genuinely open question whether it survives contact with a complete one.

articles.title: Los desafíos urgentes que asume Alberto Gamero en su esperado regreso a Millonarios
articles.standfirst: Los grandes retos de Alberto Gamero al volver a Millonarios
articles.summary: Los grandes retos de Alberto Gamero al volver a Millonarios
articles.body: Millonarios confirmó oficialmente el regreso de Alberto Gamero a la dirección técnica del equipo profesional. El estratega samario de 62 años toma las riendas del club en reemplazo de Fabián Bustos, iniciando así su segundo ciclo en el banquillo azul tras su exitoso paso entre 2020 y 2024, periodo donde conquistó tres títulos (Copa Colombia 2022, Liga BetPlay I-2023 y Superliga 2024). Aunque el equipo se encuentra en zona de clasificación en la Liga BetPlay, las directivas apostaron por un cambio de rumbo debido a las sensaciones futbolísticas que dejaba el plantel. En esta nueva etapa, Gamero asume la responsabilidad con varios desafíos prioritarios en el horizonte El primer objetivo a corto plazo es devolver la competitividad constante a la institución en el torneo local. Millonarios acumula dos ediciones consecutivas de la Liga BetPlay sin lograr avanzar a la fase final de todos contra todos. Gamero tiene la misión inmediata de asegurar un cupo en los cuadrangulares semifinales, volver a pelear por el título de liga y buscar protagonismo en la Copa Colombia. Durante su primer ciclo de cinco temporadas, Gamero le devolvió a Millonarios la identidad de juego, consolidó una importante cantera de juveniles y levantó trofeos locales. No obstante, el principal reproche hacia ese proyecto siempre fue el rendimiento en torneos de la CONMEBOL, donde el azul quedó en deuda en la Copa Libertadores y la Copa Sudamericana. En este nuevo periodo, directivos e hinchada coinciden en un único gran objetivo estratégico: recuperar el peso histórico y el protagonismo en el continente. Tras temporadas recientes en las que el club realizó un esfuerzo económico considerable para armar la plantilla, la exigencia no se limita al título local, sino a construir un proyecto competitivo capaz de plantar cara a los gigantes del fútbol suramericano. Una de las razones principales para la salida de Fabián Bustos fue el rendimiento en cancha del equipo. Pese a sumar puntos, el colectivo no ofrecía el nivel ni la propuesta deseada por la hinchada y las directivas. El director técnico buscará reactivar la fórmula táctica de posesión, presión y dinamismo que caracterizó su primera etapa, explorando al mismo tiempo variantes que le den mayor fluidez y variantes al ataque. Durante su primer periodo en el banquillo albiazul, el entrenador samario se destacó por promover a jóvenes figuras que posteriormente dieron el salto al fútbol internacional o se consolidaron en el FPC, como Óscar Cortés, Carlos Andrés Gómez, Emerson Rivaldo Rodríguez, Nicolás Arévalo y Neiser Villarreal. El nuevo proceso requerirá mirar nuevamente hacia las fuerzas básicas de la institución para nutrir al plantel profesional con nuevos talentos. El estreno oficial de Alberto Gamero en esta segunda etapa con el 'Embajador' será este domingo 6 de septiembre de 2026, cuando visite al Deportivo Pereira en Palmaseca por la novena fecha de la Liga BetPlay.

articles.title: Former WWE star John Cena reveals how his heel turn failed creatively despite the company's business success
articles.summary: WWE News: Former WWE star John Cena has admitted that his WWE heel turn has massively failed creatively, despite business success, even though the storyline del.
articles.body: Former WWE star John Cena has admitted that his WWE heel turn has massively failed creatively, despite business success, even though the storyline delivered strong business results. However, he has no regrets about agreeing to the change during his final run as an in-ring competitor. While the storyline generated considerable discussion among fans, Cena believes there is a distinction between its creative reception and its commercial performance.The context goes back to the Elimination Chamber PLE held on March 1, 2025, where John Cena turned heel for the first time in the history of WWE. During the event, the Cenation leader was badly involved in a feud with WWE champion Cody Rhodes when he refused to sell his soul to the Rock.The Final Boss and Cena were also joined by US rapper and pop sensation Travis Scott, who was invited to join the ring by Triple H. Along with Cena, Travis also launched a brutal attack against Rhodes, which left him in a pool of blood at the end of the event.John Cena acknowledged his controversial WWE heel turn during his final year as an in-ring performerFormer star John Cena has recently acknowledged his controversial WWE heel turn during his final year as an in-ring performer, which was considered a creative failure, even though the storyline delivered strong business results. He also admitted that he has no regrets about agreeing to the change during his final run as an in-ring competitor.Speaking with Graham “GSM” Matthews on Friday, Cena drew a clear line between the business results and the creative reception. While noting that WWE continued selling out arenas and posting strong viewership, but it creatively affected him.“As far as, ‘Did it work?’ There are a lot of aspects to that. From a business side, we didn’t have a seat left. People watched in numbers. I don’t know if it didn’t work from a business standpoint, but then there a creative standpoint. Sometimes, blockbuster movies are poorly reviewed by critics. I understand where, critically, people are like, ‘This isn’t what I wanted.’ Intrinsically, I would’ve loved to have a chance to literally ruin wrestling.” Cena stated.He further stated, “To wrestle so poorly that people just wanted to see me go and wanted to see a hero thwart me. We didn’t have that kind of time, and that would not have been good for business. That would’ve made people stop coming to shows and the numbers go down.”The Cenation Leader further acknowledged and revealed that he is grateful for the role, stating, “I’m grateful that I had good guidance and mentors. I’m also accountable for critiques. Long and short, I’m glad to have done it. I never asked for [the heel turn]. It wasn’t my idea. It was Paul’s idea. He asked me, and two seconds later, I said yes. Just like facing Brock or tapping out to Gunther. ‘Yes.’ That’s how I do business. Yes, just let me tell the story my way.”Cena is currently busy with "John Cena Classic," a tournament designed to pit the current WWE roster against up-and-coming stars, but there has been no further information since Cena's appearance at Backlash.Reports suggest the John Cena Classic is still planned for later this year, with a target date in December, although this has not been finalized yet and WWE isn’t ready to announce it just yet.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "No hubo lealtad": Fabián Bustos lanza duros reproches tras su salida de Millonarios
articles.standfirst: Fabián Bustos revela motivos de su salida de Millonarios: acusó temas extradeportivos y falta de lealtad
articles.summary: Fabián Bustos revela motivos de su salida de Millonarios: acusó temas extradeportivos y falta de lealtad
articles.body: La salida del técnico argentino Fabián Bustos de la dirección técnica de Millonarios sigue generando controversia en el fútbol colombiano. Tras ser desvinculado de manera imprevista del conjunto capitalino, el estratega rompió el silencio en entrevista con el programa Planeta Fútbol de Win Sports, donde dejó ver su molestia por las formas de la directiva y aseguró que su despido no respondió a criterios estrictamente deportivos. Bustos, quien estuvo siete meses al frente del equipo embajador, catalogó la forma en que se dio su salida como "totalmente atípica". El técnico remarcó que las cifras respaldaban su gestión, tras haber tomado a un equipo golpeado y ubicarlo en la pelea dentro del grupo de los ocho clasificados. "Deportivamente no había razón por los números. No son situaciones normales en el fútbol. Yo creo que fueron decisiones que no son futbolísticas... Para mí es una decisión totalmente equivocada, y el proceder de ella también", expresó Bustos. Y añade: “No me dejaron trabajar”. Durante la entrevista, el técnico argentino recordó que semanas atrás había rechazado una oferta económica tentadora del club Universitario de Deportes (Perú) para mantenerse firme en el proyecto con el equipo bogotano. Por esa razón, cuestionó la falta de reciprocidad por parte de la alta dirigencia del club. “A lo mejor sí por el juego, que no le puede gustar al dueño del club o a los dueños del club, pero deportivamente, con los números que presentaron ustedes y que todo el mundo sabe, es imposible que te saquen de un lugar así”, se refiere sobre las decisiones de los directivos de Millonarios La salida del estratega argentino se produjo de forma paralela a la negociación y llegada de Alberto Gamero al banquillo azul, un movimiento relámpago que tomó por sorpresa al entorno deportivo, considerando que el entrenador samario se encontraba negociando con Junior de Barranquilla. Aunque Bustos admitió que su propuesta de juego podía no ser del agrado de los propietarios del club, insistió en que el proceder administrativo fue equivocado y dejó una frase contundente sobre la gestión del club: "Es una institución muy linda por su gente, pero cuando tiene que tomar decisiones pensando en lo futbolístico, se equivoca mucho".

articles.title: Jefferson Lerma, fuera de la Europa League: Crystal Palace no lo inscribió para la fase de grupos
articles.standfirst: Duro golpe para Jefferson Lerma en Inglaterra: Crystal Palace tomó radical decisión con el colombiano antes de la Europa League
articles.summary: Duro golpe para Jefferson Lerma en Inglaterra: Crystal Palace tomó radical decisión con el colombiano antes de la Europa League
articles.body: El panorama de Jefferson Lerma en el fútbol británico ha dado un giro inesperado y preocupante. Tras la salida de su compatriota Daniel Muñoz rumbo al Nottingham Forest, el mediocampista vallecaucano se había quedado como la única representación colombiana en el Crystal Palace. Sin embargo, su estatus dentro del conjunto de Londres sufrió un severo revés tras conocerse las recientes decisiones del cuerpo técnico. Por determinación directa del director técnico Pierre Sage, Lerma quedó fuera de la lista oficial de convocados para disputar la UEFA Europa League en la temporada 2026/2027. La noticia cayó como un jarro de agua fría tanto en el entorno del jugador como en la prensa colombiana, considerando la experiencia y el rodaje internacional que aporta el mediocentro a la plantilla. Esta desconvocatoria no solo margina al volante de uno de los torneos continentales más prestigiosos de Europa, sino que reconfirma la pérdida de protagonismo que venía registrando en el inicio de la Premier League, donde ha sumado escasos minutos y no parece figurar entre las opciones habituales ni como recambio. El escenario actual de Lerma contrasta de manera drástica con sus campañas anteriores. Llegado al Crystal Palace en julio de 2023 procedente del Bournemouth, el colombiano no tardó en consolidarse como una pieza clave en la medular. Durante la temporada 2024/25 llegó a disputar 33 partidos de Premier League (26 de ellos como titular), y fue parte activa del plantel que levantó la FA Cup. Incluso participó en la conquista de la UEFA Conference League en la campaña 2025/2026, donde vencieron en la final al Rayo Vallecano. Con más de 160 partidos acumulados en el fútbol inglés entre su paso por Bournemouth y Crystal Palace, su rol dentro de las 'Águilas' parecía afianzado. No obstante, la llegada del nuevo curso y las decisiones de Pierre Sage han enviado una señal clara: el jugador no tendría espacio en el proyecto deportivo actual. Ante la falta de minutos y la marginación en competencias internacionales, el futuro del volante de la Selección Colombia podría dar un giro en los próximos días. Aunque el mercado en las principales ligas de Europa ya cerró y su vinculación con clubes del fútbol español no llegó a concretarse, aún existen ventanas de transferencias abiertas en diversas partes del mundo. Entre los destinos potenciales donde Lerma podría buscar rodaje antes del cierre de registros destacan: A pesar de que en declaraciones recientes el propio futbolista confesó su anhelo de vestir la camiseta del América de Cali en la Liga BetPlay, también aclaró que aún no considera que sea el momento de retornar al país. Por ello, una salida exprés hacia el exterior se perfila como la alternativa más viable para evitar un semestre relegado al banquillo en Selhurst Park.

articles.title: Josh Charnley: Leigh Leopards winger's try celebration signals contract extension
articles.summary: Super League's all-time leading try scorer Josh Charnley signs a mock contract extension during a try celebration - with his new deal announced moments later.
articles.body:
Super League's all-time leading try-scorer Josh Charnley chose an opportune moment to tell the world he has extended his stay with Leigh Leopards - signing a mock-up of a contract while celebrating a try against St Helens.

Charnley registered his 281st Super League try to open the scoring in Friday's Super League fixture against Saints, and then Leigh confirmed , external that the 35-year-old will play on into the 2027 campaign.

Former England winger Charnley said: "At the beginning of the year, I spoke to my family and said this might be my last, but coming into the year, I got my body right, so I put it on Derek [Beaumont, owner] and Lammy's [Adrian Lam, head coach] toes and said I wanted to go round again.

"I'm happy to be staying at this club and I'm grateful for the opportunity they've given me.

"It's a good club to be at - I speak about it all the time. They're going places and I'm glad to still be a part of it."

Former Wigan and Warrington player Charnley claimed the Super League try record in June, overtaking Leeds winger and former England team-mate Ryan Hall.

articles.title: Paula Josemaría y Bea González tendrán su revancha en Madrid
articles.standfirst: Las número dos volverán a cruzarse con Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo en semifinales
articles.summary: Las número dos volverán a cruzarse con Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo en semifinales
articles.body: ‘Dinamita’ y la ‘Perla’ firman una de las campañas más sólidas del circuito, pero hay un choque directo que se les ha atragantado en los últimos meses: el que les mide a Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo. Desde que las dos jóvenes promesas decidieron unir sus caminos, se han visto las caras en dos ocasiones, saldándose ambas con triunfo para la dupla número cuatro. Tras superar unos cuartos de final plácidos en el Comunidad de Madrid P1, las jugadoras entrenadas por Claudio Gilardoni dispondrán de una nueva oportunidad para revertir ese historial. Paula Josemaría y Bea González llegan además en un estado de forma óptimo. Las condiciones de la pista del Movistar Arena, sensiblemente rápidas, potencian el juego ofensivo de la malagueña y la extremeña. Su trayectoria en la capital roza la excelencia, encadenando actuaciones contundentes en cada ronda. En el cruce de cuartos de final ante Marta Ortega y Sofía Araújo exhibieron su versión más dominante. El arranque del encuentro respondió a un ritmo frenético e inalcanzable para sus oponentes. Un parcial inicial sin margen para la réplica permitió a Josemaría y González cerrar el primer set con un severo 6-0. Pese al riesgo de cierta relajación tras un parcial en blanco, la pareja número dos mantuvo la concentración en la segunda manga para certificar la victoria con un claro 6-2. Convertidas en una de las grandes sensaciones de la temporada, Fernández y Calvo buscan consolidar su momento en la capital. Tras dos pruebas previas brillantes, la joven dupla mantiene la solidez en sus compromisos sobre la moqueta madrileña. En cuartos se medían a Alejandra Alonso y Marina Guinart, un binomio llamado a exigirles al máximo, pero resolvieron el choque con una madurez impropia de su juventud. El primer parcial discurrió bajo una gran paridad y necesitó del tie-break para decantarse del lado de Fernández y Calvo. En la segunda manga imprimieron una marcha más para sellar la victoria por 7-6 y 6-2, evitando el tercer set y prolongando su racha de resultados en el circuito Premier Padel. Las semifinales de este sábado albergarán un nuevo pulso entre ambas parejas por un billete a la gran final. Un duelo clave para marcar la tendencia en el inicio de este segundo tramo del curso, donde hasta cuatro duplas pelearán por disputarle el número uno del ranking a Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea.

articles.title: Scott Gardner: They didn't get what they deserved
articles.summary: A first half goal from Charlton Athletic Under-21s condemned Leeds United Under-21s to a narrow defeat at Princes Park on Friday evening despite an encouragi...
articles.body:
A first half goal from Charlton Athletic Under-21s condemned Leeds United Under-21s to a narrow defeat at Princes Park on Friday evening despite an encouraging performance.

The Premier League Cup fixture was the Whites' second in Group I of the competition, following a goalless draw away at Stoke City, and Scott Gardner was happy with what he saw from his players.

"I thought overall, absolutely excellent," the boss complimented. "Barring one bit of quality from them once it gets to the goal, and a bit of luck inside the box for us, but in between I couldn't have asked for any more, so I'm really proud of them actually.

"I thought the game was totally connected. I don't think at any point, maybe towards the back end as we started to search for a goal, I thought we were in total control.

"All the more physical side, I thought they dealt with it incredibly well and I'm just disappointed that they didn't get what they deserved."

Gardner is confident that his side will be rewarded for their efforts in the coming games, stating: "Last week we were disappointed to lose against Liverpool, two decisions go against you, and tonight with a bit of luck at both ends, maybe you get a goal, but it's coming.

"I'm confident we'll get a result out there, a result and performance that mirror each other.

"The last two games were significantly better than the West Brom game. So it's a strange one because you don't want to be happy about losing games, but equally, we want to win a certain way, and I feel we're close."

And finally, the U21s coach praised the excellent support from the travelling Whites.

articles.title: Tim Tebow on DJ Lagway’s transfer to Baylor: ‘I think he needed a new environment’
articles.summary: It’s safe to say expectations were extremely high for Five Star Plus+ quarterback DJ Lagway when he stepped foot on Florida‘s campus in 2024. He was the No....
articles.body:
It's safe to say expectations were extremely high for Five Star Plus+ quarterback DJ Lagway when he stepped foot on Florida 's campus in 2024. He was the No. 3 ranked player in his class, and was expected to succeed quarterback Graham Mertz as the future of the program.

Following Mertz's season-ending injury in Florida 's sixth game of the season (against Tennessee ), however, the true freshman was propelled to the team's starting role. He shined across the Gators' final six games of the season, leading the program to a 5-1 record with two ranked victories (No. 9 Ole Miss and No. 22 LSU ) and a 33-8 drumming of future Florida head coach Jon Sumrall and Tulane in the Gasparilla Bowl.

Heading into last season, Lagway was expected to take the next step and evolve into not only a superstar, but a true Heisman contender in Gainesville. However, things just didn't pan out for the Willis, Texas native. Lagway, who entered the season with a few nagging injuries, was held to just 222 yards passing in Florida 's second game of the season against USF . That resulted in an 18-16 loss to the Bulls, which marked the first time ever Florida had lost to South Florida (previously 3-0).

Things didn't get better for Lagway the following week. He tossed five interceptions in a 20-10 loss to No. 3 LSU . He would go on to play in all 12 games for Florida last season, where he totaled 2,264 yards passing with 16 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. The Gators finished at 4-8, and fired head coach Billy Napier seven games into the season.

Following the season, Lagway entered the transferportal in search of a new opportunity. He landed at Baylor , where he will play for head coach Dave Aranda this season. He'll open his tenure as a Bear on Saturday against Auburn and first-year head coach Alex Golesh , who led USF to the win over the Gators last season.

Tim Tebow opens up on DJ Lagway's transfer to Baylor

Ahead of that game, however, Florida legend Tim Tebow opened up about Lagway's decision to depart the program. He proclaimed that the quarterback 'needed an opportunity', and could 'play to the best of his ability' thanks to a change in scenery.

"I think DJ needed a new opportunity," Tebow said on 'The Paul Finebaum Show.' "There was so much pressure on him. There was not enough help around him in Gainesville. When things started to spiral, there was not enough people stepping up, being able to take some of the blame. I think DJ is someone that I'll root for, because he's a very likable young man.

"He's a very good young man. He's a pretty talented young man. I just think there was way too much pressure on him to start. He needed a new environment. I think he'll play with a lot more joy, and I think when he does that, I think he'll have an opportunity to play to the best of his ability."

Lagway has full reign of a Baylor program that is coming off a disappointing 5-7 record. With both the quarterback and head coach Dave Aranda in need of a big-time bounce back season, it's hard to understate how important Saturday's game against Auburn is for the duo.

Opening the season with a win over an SEC program could be monstrous for the perception of Lagway, Aranda, and the Baylor Bears heading into back-to-back buy-games. This could potentially set up Baylor heading into Big 12 play against Colorado on Sept. 26 with an unblemished 3-0 record. Saturday's game against Auburn at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta kicks off at 3:30 PM (ET) on ABC.

articles.title: Enzo Maresca on determination to sign Enzo Fernandez and Manchester City players' reaction
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca has explained Manchester City's decision to sign Enzo Fernandez in a club-record $169.1 million move, with several teammates desperate to know i...
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca revealed Manchester City players were eagerly anticipating confirmation that Enzo Fernandez was joining, as he welcomes a 'winner' to the Manchester City locker room. The Blues dismissed any notion that they would pursue the Chelsea star at the start of the transfer window but secured a £125 million ($169.1 million) deal on its final day to cap a record summer of arrivals and departures.

Fernandez will become part of a revamped midfield at the Etihad, where upwards of £300 million ($405.5 million) has been invested in three players: Fernandez, Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

City passed up the chance to pay a marginally lower fee for Fernandez earlier in the window, but did succeed in negotiating Chelsea's £135 million ($182.5 million) asking price down in the closing hours as they ultimately delivered the club-record acquisition, as per the Manchester Evening News .

With Rodri and Bernardo Silva's summer exits anticipated, Maresca had been tracking Fernandez for some time - particularly given the player had made his willingness to leave Chelsea apparent. The two shared success together at Stamford Bridge and the manager needed no persuasion when questioned about the reasoning behind the signing.

"I know Enzo quite well. I know what he can bring to the team. He's a winner, has a winner's mentality. He knows how to win - World Cup, Club World Cup. The main thing is that, again, he's a winner," he said.

"He's a winner and when you belong to a squad and another winner arrives they are always happy. I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players in the squad were asking if he was coming or not because they want him to be with us. It's very important that he is with us and we are 100 percent happy with that."

Fernandez could make his debut as early as Saturday when they take on Frank Lampard's Coventry City at the Etihad; however, he will not feature amongst Maresca's captaincy group this season after the new boss opted to add Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma to the leadership setup instead.

Matheus Nunes is also anticipated to return to the squad following his absence from the trip to Crystal Palace, while Jeremy Doku remains on the sidelines.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz says he will take ‘long breaks’ from tennis to deal with ‘impossible’ calendar
articles.summary: World No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz has said that in the future, he will be taking longer breaks from tennis to avoid the congested schedule he faces every year.
articles.body:
World No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz has said that in the future, he will be taking longer breaks from tennis to avoid the congested schedule he faces every year.

Alcaraz is currently at the 2026 US Open, where he has reached the third round and is currently facing China's Wu Yibing at Arthur Ashe Stadium, winning the first set 6-3 while leading the second set 4-3. The Spaniard made his comeback to tennis at the ongoing Flushing Meadows after four and a half months following his recovery from a right wrist injury.

Due to the injury and his recovery, Alcaraz had to miss the French Open and Wimbledon. As a result, he has decided to take regular breaks to avoid the risk of injuries and burnout.

Carlos Alcaraz explains why he would miss tournaments deliberately

Alcaraz said that during his wrist injury, he took more time off than he originally wanted and underlined the fact that a packed calendar makes regular breaks necessary.

"I took more [time off] than I wanted, to be honest, but you know, seeing how tight is the calendar, obviously I don't want to have this break because [of] an injury," he said.

Alcaraz further added that he would be taking one to two months off in the future and will miss some tournaments as it gets difficult to play them all.

"But in the future, I'm going to take some breaks, some long breaks. Maybe not four months, but one month, two months, missing some tournaments, because it's impossible to play them all," he concluded.

Alcaraz's concern comes as his Italian rival Jannik Sinner suffered a similar fate and was ruled out of the US Open due to a right knee injury he sustained after winning the Wimbledon title in July. He is still recovering from the injury.

In addition to Sinner, several players like Jack Draper, Holger Rune and Joao Fonseca are among the absentees at this year's US Open.

Seven out of nine ATP Masters 1000 tournaments have been extended to 12 days, while only Monte Carlo and Paris have retained the traditional one-week format. As a result, taking the breaks Alcaraz was talking about could become more practical.

Bad opponent – Nothern Illinois is BAD bad, you guys – home game, good offensive line, looks like a potentially potent offense with weapons everywhere…this is a great opener. This is a great opener for the two new quarterbacks Kirk Ferentz is breaking in, too. Just no lollypop throws like I saw in Piscataway last night, please.

Iowa enters as a 31.5-point favorite on FanDuel and that doesn't seem like a crazy line. articles.title: Former Chargers cornerback breaks silence on trade to Seahawks
articles.summary: Former Chargers cornerback Avery Smith opened up about trade to the Seahawks.
articles.body:
The Chargers have made a flurry of moves since trimming the roster from 90 to 53 players.

One of those moves included trading away undrafted cornerback Avery Smith.

Smith was sent to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. In exchange, the Chargers received a 2027 sixth-round pick. The 22-year-old spoke to reporters on Thursday about the trade and admitted he was surprised by the trade for one particular reason.

"I follow football, and I haven't really heard of an undrafted free agent getting traded before the regular season," Smith said .

Smith signed with the Chargers in the spring as an undrafted free agent out of Toledo. He had a strong showing in camp; however, there was simply no room for the undrafted rookie in a packed cornerback room.

Cornerbacks like Donte Jackson, Cam Hart and Tarheeb Still had the leg up on Smith.

Prior to joining the Chargers, Smith was a standout at Toledo. He recorded 127 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss,26 passes defended, three interceptions and one forced fumble.

Smith did good work with the Chargers, and now he will look to make a name for himself in Seattle. He's among five cornerbacks that the Seahawks have on the 53-man roster.

According to Ourlads, Smith is second on the depth chart at the nickleback position.

articles.title: Criticism mounts as Buffalo Bills face backlash over reckless Josh Allen safety decision
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are under fire over the condition of their field. Experts claim the team put Josh Allen at unnecessary risk by playing him on a surface tha...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are under fire over the condition of their field. Experts claim the team put Josh Allen at unnecessary risk by playing him on a surface that was falling apart.

The Athletic's Tim Graham revealed this week that the team had to tear out the grass installed in October 2025. The roots never took hold, and large chunks of sod came loose during the two pre-season games.

Critics are asking how the team allowed the reigning league MVP to play in that state.

Experts slam the call to play Josh Allen

Allen was on the field for only a couple of series under new head coach Joe Brady. In that short time he was taken down twice, including one sack.

Tony Dick, a sports management professor and former Browns assistant head groundskeeper, watched the film and did not hold back.

'Yes, natural turf is safer in a perfect setting,' Dick said. 'But if you have the situation like you have in Buffalo, and I went back and watched the film, you cannot tell me that field was safer than the artificial turf they just left.'

'I'm never putting Josh Allen on a field in that condition.'

The Bills have now decided to resod the entire field.

Matteo Bartolotta, whose company M&K Turf works with the Bills' grounds staff, said the move was the right one even if the timing is tight.

'It's a lot more common to replace sod fields than people think,' he said. 'We do have the three-game stretch coming. If they wait, with that NFL test of playability, they might not have passed it if the conditions got worse. It's not cheap, but I think it was the right choice.'

Buffalo host the Detroit Lions on Thursday Night Football in under two weeks. One unnamed agronomist is already worried about the week after, when the Los Angeles Chargers come to town.

'They will have a difficult time. There's so much going wrong, and there's so little time,' they said. 'If that field makes it through the second game, I'll be shocked.'

The response comes after Allen was voted the No. 2 player in the NFL by his peers, making him the top-ranked quarterback in the league.

The Bills cannot afford to lose him. The field is being fixed, but the questions over how it got this bad are not going away.

articles.title: Chicago Bears: Restructure Contract of 30-Year-Old Starter
articles.summary: Chicago Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards faces a make-or-break 2026 season as he could be released this offseason if things do not go according to plan. Edwards...
articles.body:
Chicago Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards faces a make-or-break 2026 season as he could be released this offseason if things do not go according to plan. Edwards is coming off an underwhelming 2025 campaign, during which he battled a hamstring injury that he later aggravated, along with a broken hand and a fractured fibula, which was sustained in the Wild Card Round, limiting him to a career-low 11 games. In addition, he missed the first week and a half of training camp with a minor calf injury but participated in the last month.

Edwards technically enters the first year of his two-year, $20 million contract. He is scheduled to earn a fully guaranteed $8.25 million base salary and $8.5 million in cash while carrying a $10.833 million cap hit in 2026, per Over The Cap .

The Chicago Bears restructure the contract of a 30-year-old starter

According to Field Yates of ESPN, the Bears have restructured T.J. Edwards' contract. Per Spotrac, the front office converted $6.95 million of Edwards' base salary into a signing bonus, freeing up $3,475,000 in cap space. As a result, his base salary drops to the league minimum of $1.3 million, while his cap hit dips to $7,358,333. Additionally, the $6.95 million prorated signing bonus will be spread evenly over two years at $3,475,000 per year, increasing his 2027 dead cap to $5,808,334.

Because Edwards' contract was restructured, he may not be released next offseason, as the dead cap increased. However, a standard release would save $8.5 million in cap space, which is still a sizeable amount.

articles.title: Chris Sutton: Liverpool ‘got away with one’ early in second half after ‘clumsy’ moment
articles.summary: Chris Sutton claimed that Liverpool ‘may have got away’ with a potential red card offence at Portman Road on Friday night.The Reds surged into a 2-0 lead aga...
articles.body:
Chris Sutton claimed that Liverpool 'may have got away' with a potential red card offence at Portman Road on Friday night.

The Reds surged into a 2-0 lead against Ipswich inside nine minutes thanks to a brace of Alexander Isak goals, both of which were set up by Cody Gakpo , although the home side asked a few questions of the visitors later in the first half.

Seven minutes after the interval, Jeremy Jacquet was shown a yellow card by Darren England for a collison with Tractor Boys striker Emersson near the halfway line.

Sutton: Jacquet 'got away with one' for tripping Emersson

That prompted Sutton to say on co-commentary for Sky Sports that the Liverpool defender 'has had the odd clumsy moment in this game' , perhaps referring to a first-half moment of hesitation between him and Alisson Becker inside the Reds' penalty area.

Just a couple of minutes after being booked, the 21-year-old took a heavy touch near the sideline and gave the Ipswich striker the chance to steal the ball off him, with the Frenchman then tripping his opponent but not being penalised by the referee.

Sutton felt that the official could easily have reached for his pocket again, saying: "He [Jacquet] needs to be careful! Liverpool have got away with one there. Gary O'Neil is furious."

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Jacquet taking a bit of a risk just after being booked

Jacquet has looked like a tremendous addition for the Reds in his early appearances since his move from Rennes, making a crucial block in the 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest last weekend.

However, the French defender has had a couple of uncertain moments at Portman Road tonight, and on another occasion he mightn't have got off with a potential second foul (and yellow card) on Emersson.

It's all part of the learning process for the 21-year-old in his first few games in England, and while he'll need to learn quickly, we don't doubt that he has the ability to do so.

Liverpool had their own grievance with the officials later in the second half when Dominik Szoboszlai's shirt was tugged by Leif Davis inside the penalty area, but the Hungarian had strayed offside in the build-up to that incident, thus overriding any potential spot kick.

Both head coaches might have their say on various refereeing decisions from this match, but at the time of writing, the Reds just need to keep their concentration and see their 2-0 lead through to full-time.

articles.title: Emotional Taylor steps on to the scales one final time
articles.summary: Katie Taylor and Flora Pili weigh in under the light-welterweight limit at a sun-kissed Trinity College in Dublin before they fight for the undisputed title...
articles.body:
Katie Taylor has taken her final week as a professional boxer in her stride.

Each media event has been ticked off with the kind of composure and poise she has displayed in the ring for over two decades.

Dublin blessed Taylor and opponent Flora Pili with some early autumn sun as they weighed in at Trinity College before Saturday's undisputed light-welterweight battle at a sold-out Croke Park.

Taylor has not missed weight once in her 26-fight career and she was not going to buck the trend as she was greeted by adoring fans - many whom have followed her career since she won Olympic gold in 2012.

The announcement of the weights - both coming in just under the 10st (63.5kg) limit - was almost immaterial.

All 80,000 tickets for Saturday's undisputed light-welterweight fight have been long snapped up and demand for Friday's ceremonial weigh-in proved just as high.

Supporters packed into Trinity College, a seat of higher learning founded in 1592 by Queen Elizabeth I, to catch a glimpse of the queen of Irish sport.

Women were not permitted to study at Trinity College until 1904 but Taylor, who has smashed barriers for women in and out of the ring - was the star attraction.

Trinity's old library is an attraction in its own right, home to the Book of Kells - an illustrated manuscript, which contains the four Gospels of the New Testament in Latin - but those in its grounds were there for their own piece of history on this final fight week of Taylor's illustrious career.

The 40-year-old, two-weight undisputed champion, may not be a huge fan of the fight week obligations and making weight is certainly an aspect to the sport that will not be missed, but this was an opportunity to soak it all in one last time.

Pili has been the perfect guest all week, complimentary and polite, but the Frenchwoman is not here to be a tourist and there was an air of confidence as she hit the scales.

The 29-year-old has stitched together a perfect record of 12 wins and has an opportunity to raise her own reputation if she can pull of a major upset.

It is Pili's biggest night, an opportunity to catapult herself into the upper echelons of the fight game, but an also occasion she has never experienced and looked a little bemused as she stepped on to the scales.

As violinists played Irish folk song 'Óró, sé do bheatha 'bhaile' [Óró - you are welcome home], Taylor appeared to a rapturous reception and the fighters went through the formalities, all smiles and handshakes.

Taylor rarely displays emotion in fight week but she has shown a different side of the past couple of days as the curtain starts to fall on her illustrious career.

The Bray fighter, who had her mother Bridgit close by, choked up at times and appeared as she delivered her final messages.

"I'm so excited. I've been saying all week how I grateful I am for this opportunity. I've been dreaming of this for the last few years and now it's just one day away. It's just one day away from ending my career in my dream venue of Croke Park," Taylor told the crowd after her final face-off.

"All these amazing people are here today and I'm blown away. I can't wait to step in there and I want to put in a performance worthy of everyone's support.

"You have carried me through the Rio Olympics, London Olympics and throughout my professional career. Thank you."

Both fighters can now breathe a little easier as it is onto the task at hand.

The buzz that has steadily built all week will reach a crescendo when they make their way to the ring around 22:00 BST on Saturday, and while the occasion remains grand, the destination of the title belts remains the priority.

"My mind is very much focused on the fight," Taylor reiterated.

"I have a tough challenger in front of me but I've built a reputation of taking tough fights - why treat my last fight any differently?

"Tomorrow is going to be an amazing celebration. I'm super proud to represent this amazing country. Let's go one more time."
authors: David Mohan - BBC Sport NI journalist

articles.title: Texas A&M unveils statue honoring R.C. Slocum
articles.summary: Texas A&M unveiled the statue of legendary football head coach R.C. Slocum on Friday. Take a look here.
articles.body:
The Texas A&M Aggies will open the 2026 season against the Missouri State Bears on Saturday at Kyle Field, and they unveiled a statue of former head coach R.C. Slocum on Friday ahead of the game.

Slocum served as the head coach from 1989-2002, compiling a record of 123-47-2 to become the winningest coach in program history. The statue stands outside the north end of Kyle Field beside the All-American Towers and is 10 feet tall.

Current head coach Mike Elko discussed the statue earlier this week, mentioning how he excited he was for it and what Slocum means to the Aggies.

"To me, I view him as a legend," he said . "That's how I've always seen him. I appreciate what he means to this community. I appreciate what he means to this football program," Elko said. "I have a ton of respect and admiration for who he is, and I want to make sure he knows he's always welcomed around. This is his home. … He means so much to this university."

Here is a look at the statue, which was sculpted by Steven White.

Slocum is by far the most successful head coach in Texas A&M history, leading them to three straight Southwest Conference championships from 1991 to 1993 and a Big 12 title in 2998. He was named the SWC Coach of the Year three times and inducted into the Texas Sports Hall of Fame and College Football Hall of Fame.

He continued to help Texas A&M even after he stopped coaching, serving as special adviser to Texas A&M's president. He also served as Texas A&M's interim athletic director in 2019 and 2024.

articles.title: Chargers predicted to swing bold J.J. McCarthy trade that would make perfect sense
articles.summary: This might seem wild at first glance, but it actually makes a lot of sense.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers have already found their franchise quarterback with Justin Herbert. There really isn't a need to go investing into the QB position unless it's for a backup.

In most cases, a veteran journeyman like Trey Lance is more than good enough. If Herbert goes down, the season is likely over anyway. But that doesn't mean the Chargers shouldn't still look for better QBs.

That's what Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report is predicting the Chargers will do, as he predicts they'll trade for Minnesota Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy in a very bold trade that actually makes perfect sense.

Chargers predicted to trade for J.J. McCarthy in move that'd make sense

"Chargers get: QB J.J. McCarthy. Vikings get: 2028 5th-round pick," Knox predicts. "While this isn't a trade that would impact the starting lineup of either the Vikings or the Chargers, it would bring an end to the McCarthy experiment in Minnesota."

Trading for McCarthy after his lost rookie season due to an injury and his very poor 2025 season as the Vikings' starter would not make a lot of sense. At least, for most teams.

The Chargers are different. McCarthy wouldn't sniff the starting lineup for the Chargers, likely even if Herbert went down with an injury. He's purely a backup in this hypothetical scenario.

But for McCarthy and the Chargers, this is about as good a landing spot as he could ask for to revive his NFL career. He's still 23 years old, and the former Michigan quarterback would reunite with Jim Harbaugh after their time in Michigan together.

Besides, McCarthy had only 10 games in the NFL in his two seasons, and he is under contract on his rookie deal for the 2026 and 2027 NFL seasons.

The Chargers are one of the few teams with Harbaugh, Mike McDaniel, and a solid starter and backup ahead of McCarthy that'd make perfect sense for McCarthy in a trade.

A 2028 fifth-round pick is a little expensive for how bad McCarthy has looked at times, but to take a flyer on a cheap, young, and likely still talented QB is worth the chance.

This prediction from Knox would make perfect sense and give the Chargers the high-upside developmental QB they could benefit from adding at quite a cheap cost.

articles.title: Cumberland boys soccer to resume season after 'bullying/hazing incident'
articles.summary: The superintendent of schools said "several" players who were involved in the off-campus incident have been 'consequenced' per district policy
articles.body:
The Cumberland boys soccer team will resume its regular schedule after what the superintendent of schools described as "a bullying and/or hazing incident" took place and the players involved have been disciplined.

Superintendent Philip D. Thornton told The Providence Journal that the incident took place at a private home and involved "several members of the boys soccer team." Once school officials learned of the incident, he added that the "students were consequenced per the [Cumberland High School] Handbook & Athletic Handbook," but said he could not disclose individual student disciplines.

According to the district's athletic handbook , which was approved by the School Committee on July 16 of this year, hazing is defined as "any conduct or method of initiation" by any student organization that "willfully or recklessly endangers the physical or mental health of any student or other person."

The policy also states that "Coaches are responsible to make sure these types of activities do not occur on their team."

Under the handbook's "Student-Athlete Code of Conduct," penalties start with a one-week suspension from all team activities for a first offense and become more punitive with each subsequent offense. A second offense could mean a season-long suspension from the sport, a third offense could trigger a year-long ban from all athletics and a fourth is punishable by permanent suspension from all athletics at the high school.

In a message to parents dated Thursday, Sept. 3, Thornton had said, "The district is investigating an incident involving members of the Cumberland High School Boys Soccer Team. As this is a sensitive matter involving students, no further information is available at this time."

Cumberland had been scheduled to play at North Kingstown on Wednesday, Sept. 2, but that game was postponed . A post on the Clippers' Facebook page read, "Due to unforeseen circumstances, today's game and practices have been postponed."

Cumberland is set to play again on Wednesday, Sept. 9, when it hosts Bishop Hendricken, and Thornton said Friday that the team "will play its regular schedule for the fall."

articles.title: Virginia Tech football vs. VMI: Preview, betting odds, how to watch

articles.body:
It's finally here. The Virginia Tech Hokies will begin the 2026 season on Saturday, when the VMI Keydets make the short trip down Interstate 81 to Lane Stadium. It will be the first meeting since 1984, when the Hokies won 54-7. Believe it or not, the Hokies and Keydets were once conference rivals in the old Southern Conference from 1924-64.

The series actually began in 1894, and from 1913-74, the annual battle was played at the old Victory Stadium in Roanoke on Thanksgiving Day. It was called the Military Classic of the South.

As for Saturday's game, much has changed since these schools last faced off. That last game took place Oct. 6, 1984, in Norfolk, with the Hokies winning 54-7.

While Saturday's game is the season opener, the Keydets opened last week at Idaho State and lost 38-10.

The Keydets may be overmatched, but they could present a unique challenge. They run the triple option, something head coach James Franklin was asked about this week. It's been a while since the Hokies faced the old Georgia Tech teams coached by Paul Johnson. So, there are no real data points to see how Brent Pry's defense will play the option. VMI has a new coach, too, Ashley Ingram, who comes to Lexington from Navy, where he was very familiar with the triple option.

Saturday is Ethan Grunkemeyer's first game for the Hokies under center. Grunkemeyer officially won the job earlier this week, but that was never in question.

Virginia Tech is a huge favorite in this game. Here are the full betting odds for Saturday's game, including how you can watch, listen to on the radio, or stream.

articles.title: Serie A | Genoa 1-4 Como: Fabregas cool comeback victory
articles.summary: Como fought back from a debut Milutin Osmajic goal to crush Genoa 4-1, including an Assane Diao brace, Martin Baturina and Nico Paz, with Moise Kean providin...
articles.body:
Como fought back from a debut Milutin Osmajic goal to crush Genoa 4-1, including an Assane Diao brace, Martin Baturina and Nico Paz, with Moise Kean providing an assist.

The Lariani were fresh from a 2-1 victory away to Napoli , plus deadline day signings Moise Kean and Robert Sanchez on the bench waiting for their debuts. Only Jayden Addai remained on the treatment table. Genoa were in crisis after losing to both Napoli and Lazio without scoring a goal, as Lorenzo Venturino, Joi Nuredini, Hamed Traore and Elias Havel were still out of action, but Djibril Sow and Milutin Osmajic got their first starts.

GENOA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 04: Cesc Fabregas, Manager of Como, looks on before the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Como 1907 at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on September 04, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

Justin Bijlow fingertipped a Yan Couto curler out from under the bar, then got his glove to a Nico Paz screamer from distance, but it was Genoa who took the lead against the run of play.

Lorenzo Colombo burst down the left against a high Como line and rolled it across for former Preston North End striker Osmajic to get ahead of Trevoh Chalobah and sweep in from close range.

GENOA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 04: Milutin Osmajic of Genoa celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Como 1907 at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on September 04, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

Como drew level when Martin Baturina drilled a right-foot strike into the far bottom corner from well outside the penalty area.

GENOA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 04: Martin Baturina of Como scores his team's first goal during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Como 1907 at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on September 04, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

The game was turned on its head as Leo Ostigard only grazed his head to an Alex Valle cross, allowing Assane Diao to keep his volley down at the back post.

Como went into the break 3-1 up, as after a long spell of possession, Yan Couto dinked a ball over the top for Nico Paz, who took a touch with his left foot, let it bounce, and fired into the near top corner with his right.

GENOA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 04: Nico Paz of Como scores his team's third goal under pressure from Johan Vasquez of Genoa during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Como 1907 at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on September 04, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

Tasos Douvikas saw his header skim the bar before making way for debutant Moise Kean, while Kingsley Ehizibue came on for his first Genoa appearance too.

It was very nearly 1-4 when Nico Paz gathered a weak clearance and smashed his first-time strike onto the upright from the edge of the area.

Kean made his mark on his debut, combining with Maxence Caqueret in midfield to sprint forward, then generously rolling across for Diao to finish with the angled drive and complete his brace.

Junior Messias threatened an audacious goal with his back-heel flick just wide on a corner in the final minute, but Genoa have lost their first three games of the Serie A season.

articles.title: Sean McVay: I look at Stetson Bennett, Ty Simpson as "2A, 2B"
articles.summary: The Rams released a depth chart that shows Stetson Bennett as the team's second quarterback and first-round pick Ty Simpson as their third quarterback, but h...
articles.body:
The Rams released a depth chart that shows Stetson Bennett as the team's second quarterback and first-round pick Ty Simpson as their third quarterback, but head coach Sean McVay said things are less clear cut than that would make it appear.

McVay said that he has not made a decision about who will be active for Thursday's game against the 49ers because he views the two quarterbacks on equal footing when it comes to the competition to be the next man up behind Matthew Stafford.

"I'll tell you when I decide who is going to be the actual two in the game," McVay said, via the team's website. "I've talked to the players about it, but that's something that they're both going to continue to train regardless of who it ends up being up and who is the emergency third. I look at it as both of those guys are going to play, but you saw, we listed Stetson as the two, Ty as the three. But I look at it as the 2A, 2B and we'll see how we approach the game."

McVay added that he doesn't "want to necessarily say that whatever we do in Week 1 is how it stays throughout the year," so the backup spot could be a fluid one and the Rams will be hoping that neither player sees the field outside of garbage time between now and February.
